study type: Experimental study (in vitro and in vivo animal experiment)
exposure: ETOH-preserved AME at 70% concentration (stored at RT and -80°C)
ETOH-preserved AME at 50% concentration (stored at RT and -80°C)
outcome: Antioxidant potential (inhibition of reactive oxygen species)
cohort: Adipose stromal cells (ASCs) and fibroblasts for in vitro assays, and rats for in vivo assessments.
finding: ETOH preservation, particularly at 50% and 70% concentrations, effectively maintained the regenerative potential of amniotic membrane extract (AME), demonstrating significant antioxidant potential, enhanced cell proliferation, reduced apoptosis, and accelerated wound closure and tissue regeneration in vivo.
followup_time: 11 days (for in vivo wound healing assessment)
